# Memo 1 — Deductibility of operating costs

**To:** File
**Re:** Whether the client's operating costs are currently deductible

## Analysis

The general rule is in section 162. A taxpayer may deduct the ordinary and
necessary expenses of carrying on a trade or business. The parallel rule for
income is in I.R.C. § 61.

Some commentators cite § 162A for the proposition that advertising costs are
always deductible. That is not a real provision.

The limitation on illegal payments appears at § 162(z), and the definition of a
United States person is at § 7701(a)(30)(A).

Capital expenditures are governed by 26 U.S.C. § 263, and the uniform
capitalization rules by § 263A. Compare § 263(a)(9), which does not exist, and § 263(q), which does not
either.

Section 4 of the Code was repealed long ago, and § 1000 is reserved.

See also Rev. Rul. 2019-24 and Commissioner v. Groetzinger, 480 U.S. 23 (1987).

Section 7 of the Agreement is not a tax citation at all, and neither is
section 3 of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.
